messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran a 2k-sample slice (multi-turn helpdesk prompts) comparing model-x-13b int8 vs int4 on the chat stack. Posting the short summary here so we can decide rollout knobs.

alex: Nice, can you drop the key numbers (latency, cost, and the quality delta)?

maria: Sure. Raw numbers from the slice (avg over requests):
```
int8: p50 120ms, p95 250ms, cost per 1k tokens = $0.042, convo-F1 = 0.842
int4: p50 140ms, p95 320ms, cost per 1k tokens = $0.028, convo-F1 = 0.811
delta: -3.1% absolute F1, ~33% cost savings
```

sam: Product question — that F1 drop how visible is in error type? small hallucinations or critical failures?

maria: Mostly verbosity / minor factual hallucinations in follow-ups. When prompt chain >800 tokens we see more drift. Primary failure mode: reduced confidence on entity extraction -> downstream formatting issues. Not catastrophic for casual chat but matters for structured outputs.

jing: Ops note — int4 nodes had ~12% higher KV-cache eviction in our test config which explains p95 bump. If we increase cache size latency goes back ~30ms but increases cost slightly.

alex: So trade-offs: ~33% token cost reduction vs ~3% F1 loss and a latency tail hit. Any targeted prompts where int4 held up fine?

maria: Yes — short-form Q/A (<200 tokens) almost identical. Int4 breaks when: (a) multi-step extraction, (b) long priming with many examples. We profiled by turn depth and saw quality curve drop after 3 turns.

eval-bot: Auto-report: A/B on 2k slice. Stat test (bootstrap) shows quality delta significant (p<0.01) on long-turn subset (n=540), not significant on short-turn subset (n=1460). Signal: entity-F1 most affected.

sam: For GTN we need a recommendation: default to int4 for <=200 token flows, fallback to int8 for longer flows? Also consider sticky routing by user tier.

maria: Proposed rollout plan:
- default model variant = int4 for short-response routes (<=200 tokens output)
- route to int8 when request.turn_count >= 3 OR output_length_estimate >= 800 tokens
- enable conservative KV-cache bump (+20%) on int4 hosts to reduce tail; monitor latency cost delta
- add a prompt-sensitivity eval for structured outputs to guard regressions

jing: Ops checklist: we can add the routing flag and cache change behind a feature-flag. Need 2h infra maintenance window to push cache sizing safely.

alex: Can we quantify expected unit economics after routing? Rough calc?

maria: Quick back-of-envelope: assume 70% short flows -> avg token cost = 0.7*0.028 + 0.3*0.042 = $0.0334 per 1k tokens (~20% savings overall). With KV bump the cost for int4 path might go up ~6% -> still ~14% net savings.

sam: That seems acceptable if we catch structured-output regressions. Add a canary on 5% traffic and evaluation hooks.

maria: Agreed. I'll open the rollout PR and attach the slice + eval checklist. TL;DR: int4 is viable for short-turn chat, fallback to int8 for longer/structured. Canary + prompt-level eval required. :+1:

alex: Thanks — please ping when PR is up and we can schedule the canary. :rocket:
